$comment: Output goes to public/wasm so the module is served as a static asset with
the same immutable caching every other build artefact gets, rather than
through a route that would invoke a function to serve a fixed file.
The .wasm is committed. That is deliberate: it means `pnpm build` needs no
second toolchain, CI does not compile it, and a Vercel deploy cannot fail
because an AssemblyScript version drifted — the same reasoning that moved
the fonts into the repo in P12. `pnpm wasm:build` regenerates it, and a
test asserts the committed binary matches the source it claims to be.
